---
title: "Notation"
---

This site uses the book's notation, so you can move between the two. Symbols are grouped by the Part where they first appear, in chapter order; each is listed once, where it is introduced, unless a later chapter gives it a new meaning. The book reuses some letters for different things in different chapters; [the last section](#overloaded) lists them.

For the key equations themselves, see the [cheat sheets](cheatsheets.qmd).

## Introduction and Part I: probabilistic reasoning {#part1}

| Symbol | Meaning | First used |
|---|---|---|
| $r_t$ | Reward received at step $t$ | Ch 1 |
| $a^*$ | The action with the highest expected utility | Ch 1 |
| $P(x)$ | Probability mass function (discrete): the probability that $X = x$ | Ch 2 |
| $p(x)$ | Probability density function (continuous); probabilities are areas under it | Ch 2 |
| $\operatorname{cdf}(x)$ | Cumulative distribution function, $P(X \le x)$ | Ch 2 |
| $\mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu, \sigma^2)$ | Gaussian with mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$; $\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{x} \mid \boldsymbol\mu, \boldsymbol\Sigma)$ is the multivariate version | Ch 2 |
| $\mathcal{U}(x \mid a, b)$ | Uniform distribution on $[a, b]$ | Ch 2 |
| $\rho_i$ | Weight of component $i$ in a mixture | Ch 2 |
| $x^0$, $x^1$ | The two values of a binary variable: no, yes | Ch 2 |
| $P(x \mid y)$ | Conditional probability of $x$ given $y$ | Ch 2 |
| $\theta_1$, $\theta_2$ | Threshold and softness of a sigmoid conditional | Ch 2 |
| $x_{1:n}$ | The values $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ | Ch 2 |
| $\mathrm{pa}(x_i)$ | Values of the parents of $X_i$ in a Bayesian network | Ch 2 |
| $(X \perp Y \mid Z)$ | $X$ and $Y$ are conditionally independent given $Z$ | Ch 2 |
| $q$, $e$, $h$ | Query, evidence, and hidden variables in an inference problem | Ch 3 |
| $\phi$ | A factor: a table over some variables (a CPT, or any partial product) | Ch 3 |
| $P(c \mid o_{1:n})$ | Naive Bayes posterior of class $c$ given observations $o_1, \ldots, o_n$ | Ch 3 |
| $w$ | Likelihood weight of a sample | Ch 3 |
| $x_{-i}$ | All variables except $x_i$ | Ch 3 |
| $\boldsymbol{\mu}_{a \mid b}$, $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{a \mid b}$ | Mean and covariance of Gaussian block $\mathbf{a}$ given block $\mathbf{b}$ | Ch 3 |
| $\theta$ | Model parameters, such as CPT entries | Ch 4 |
| $\ell(\theta)$ | Log-likelihood of the data under parameters $\theta$ | Ch 4 |
| $m_{ijk}$ | Count of records with variable $i$ at value $k$ and its parents at combination $j$ | Ch 4 |
| $\hat\theta$ | An estimate of $\theta$ | Ch 4 |
| $\mathrm{Beta}(\theta \mid \alpha, \beta)$ | Beta distribution over a probability $\theta$; $\alpha$, $\beta$ act as pseudocounts | Ch 4 |
| $\mathrm{Dir}(\theta_{1:n} \mid \alpha_{1:n})$ | Dirichlet distribution over $n$ probabilities that sum to 1 | Ch 4 |
| $\phi$, $h$ | Kernel and bandwidth in kernel density estimation | Ch 4 |
| $G$, $D$ | A graph (network structure) and a dataset | Ch 5 |
| $\ln P(G \mid D)$ | Bayesian score of graph $G$ on data $D$ | Ch 5 |
| $\Gamma(x)$ | Gamma function; $\Gamma(n) = (n-1)!$ for whole numbers | Ch 5 |
| $\alpha_{ijk}$, $\alpha_{ij0}$, $m_{ij0}$ | Pseudocount for a cell, and the row totals of pseudocounts and counts | Ch 5 |
| $q_i$, $r_i$ | Number of parent combinations and number of values of variable $i$ | Ch 5 |
| $\kappa$ | Equivalent sample size of a BDeu prior | Ch 5 |
| $\mathrm{pa}_G(x_i)$ | Parents of $x_i$ in graph $G$ | Ch 5 |
| $A \succ B$, $A \sim B$, $A \succeq B$ | $A$ preferred to $B$; indifferent; at least as good | Ch 6 |
| $[S_1 : p_1; \ldots; S_n : p_n]$ | Lottery: outcome $S_i$ with probability $p_i$ | Ch 6 |
| $U(S)$ | Utility of outcome $S$ | Ch 6 |
| $S_\top$, $S_\bot$ | Best and worst outcomes, used to scale utility to $[0, 1]$ | Ch 6 |
| $x_{\text{ce}}$ | Certainty equivalent: the sure amount worth the same as a gamble | Ch 6 |
| $\lambda$ | Risk-aversion parameter of exponential utility $1 - e^{-\lambda x}$ | Ch 6 |
| $EU(a \mid o)$, $EU^*(o)$ | Expected utility of action $a$ given observation $o$; its maximum over actions | Ch 6 |
| $\mathrm{VOI}(O' \mid o)$ | Value of information of observing $O'$, given $o$ | Ch 6 |

## Part II: sequential problems {#part2}

| Symbol | Meaning | First used |
|---|---|---|
| $\mathcal{S}$ | State space | Ch 7 |
| $\mathcal{A}$ | Action space | Ch 7 |
| $T(s' \mid s, a)$ | Transition model: probability of reaching $s'$ from $s$ after action $a$ | Ch 7 |
| $R(s, a)$ | Expected reward for taking action $a$ in state $s$ | Ch 7 |
| $\gamma$ | Discount factor, $0 \le \gamma \le 1$ | Ch 7 |
| $\pi$ | Policy: maps states to actions | Ch 7 |
| $U^\pi(s)$ | Value (utility) of state $s$ under policy $\pi$ | Ch 7 |
| $U^*(s)$ | Optimal value of state $s$ | Ch 7 |
| $U_k$ | Value estimate after $k$ sweeps of value iteration | Ch 7 |
| $Q(s, a)$ | Action value: reward for $a$ in $s$ plus the discounted value $U$ of where you land | Ch 7 |
| $A(s, a)$ | Advantage: $Q(s, a) - U(s)$ | Ch 7 |
| $\mathbf{T}^\pi$, $\mathbf{R}^\pi$ | Transition matrix and reward vector with the policy's action fixed in each state | Ch 7 |
| $\lVert U \rVert_\infty$ | Largest absolute entry, $\max_s \lvert U(s) \rvert$ | Ch 7 |
| $\delta$, $\epsilon$ | Bellman-residual threshold and target accuracy in value iteration | Ch 7 |
| $U_\theta(s)$, $Q_\theta(s, a)$ | Parametric (approximate) value and action value functions with parameters $\theta$ | Ch 8 |
| $S = s_{1:m}$ | Sample states where approximate value iteration does backups | Ch 8 |
| $\beta(s)$ | Basis functions (features), or local weights, so that $U_\theta(s) = \theta^\top \beta(s)$ | Ch 8 |
| $d(s, s')$, $k(s, s')$ | Distance between states, and a kernel (larger for closer states) | Ch 8 |
| $\sigma$ | Width of a Gaussian kernel | Ch 8 |
| $X$, $X^+$ | Feature matrix (row $i$ is $\beta(s_i)^\top$) and its pseudoinverse | Ch 8 |
| $d$ | Search depth (planning horizon) of an online planner | Ch 9 |
| $U_d(s)$ | Value of $s$ from a depth-$d$ search | Ch 9 |
| $\underline{U}(s)$, $\overline{Q}(s, a)$, $\overline{U}(s)$ | Lower bound on values; upper bounds on action values and values (admissible heuristic) | Ch 9 |
| $m$ | Number of samples (sparse sampling) or simulations (MCTS, heuristic search) | Ch 9 |
| $N(s, a)$, $N(s)$ | Visit counts in Monte Carlo tree search | Ch 9 |
| $c$ | Exploration constant in UCB1 | Ch 9 |
| $\delta$ | Residual threshold for a state to count as solved | Ch 9 |
| $a_{1:d}$ | An open-loop sequence of actions | Ch 9 |
| $\pi_\theta$, $U(\theta)$ | A policy with parameters $\theta$, and its expected return | Ch 10 |
| $\tau$, $R(\tau)$, $p_\pi(\tau)$ | A trajectory, its discounted return, and its probability under $\pi$ | Ch 10 |
| $b(s)$ | Initial state distribution (for policy search) | Ch 10 |
| $\alpha$, $c$, $\epsilon$ | Step size, its reduction factor, and the stopping step size (Hooke–Jeeves) | Ch 10 |
| $m_{\text{elite}}$ | Number of elite samples kept each iteration | Ch 10 |
| $p(\theta \mid \psi)$ | Search distribution over policy parameters, with parameters $\psi$ | Ch 10 |
| $w^{(i)}$ | Rank-shaped weight of the $i$-th best sample | Ch 10 |
| $\nabla U(\theta)$ | Policy gradient: how the expected return changes with each parameter | Ch 11 |
| $\delta$, $e_i$ | Finite-difference step, and the unit vector along parameter $i$ | Ch 11 |
| $\Delta\Theta$, $\Delta U$ | Matrix of parameter perturbations (one per row) and the resulting changes in $U$ | Ch 11 |
| $\pi_\theta(a \mid s)$ | Probability (or density) that the policy takes action $a$ in state $s$ | Ch 11 |
| $\nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a \mid s)$ | Score of an action: the direction that makes it more likely | Ch 11 |
| $r_{\text{to-go}}^{(k)}$ | Reward-to-go: discounted reward from step $k$ on | Ch 11 |
| $r_{\text{base}}(s)$ | Baseline subtracted from the reward-to-go | Ch 11 |
| $F_\theta$ | Fisher information matrix of the policy's trajectory distribution | Ch 12 |
| $D_{\text{KL}}(p \,\Vert\, q)$ | Kullback–Leibler divergence from $p$ to $q$ | Ch 12 |
| $\epsilon$ | Trust-region size (KL or step budget); PPO's clipping range | Ch 12 |
| $f(\theta, \theta')$, $g(\theta, \theta')$ | TRPO's surrogate objective and surrogate KL constraint | Ch 12 |
| $b_{\gamma,\theta}(s)$ | Discounted state-visitation distribution of $\pi_\theta$ | Ch 12 |
| $w = \pi_{\theta'}(a \mid s) / \pi_\theta(a \mid s)$ | Probability ratio (importance weight) | Ch 12 |
| $U_\phi(s)$, $Q_\phi(s, a)$ | The critic: a value function with parameters $\phi$ | Ch 13 |
| $\delta_k$ | Temporal difference residual $r_k + \gamma U(s_{k+1}) - U(s_k)$ | Ch 13 |
| $\hat A^{(k)}$, $\hat A^{\text{GAE}}$ | $k$-step and generalized advantage estimates | Ch 13 |
| $\lambda$ | GAE weight between TD residuals ($\lambda = 0$) and full returns ($\lambda = 1$) | Ch 13 |
| $\nabla_\theta \pi_\theta(s)$ | Jacobian of a deterministic policy (one column per action component) | Ch 13 |
| $\pi_{\text{MCTS}}$, $U_{\text{MCTS}}$, $\eta$ | Tree search's visit-count policy (sharpened by $\eta$) and value | Ch 13 |
| $f(\pi)$ | A performance metric of policy $\pi$: the expected trajectory metric | Ch 14 |
| $f_{\text{traj}}$, $f_{\text{step}}$, $f_{\text{state}}$ | Metric of a trajectory, of one step, and its expected total from a state | Ch 14 |
| $b(s_1)$ | Start (initial state) distribution; in Ch 19 on, $b$ is a belief | Ch 14 |
| $\text{SE} = \hat\sigma/\sqrt n$ | Standard error of a sample mean; divided by $\hat\mu$, the relative standard error | Ch 14 |
| $P'(\tau)$, $P^*(\tau)$ | Proposal distribution for importance sampling; the optimal (zero-variance) proposal | Ch 14 |
| $w = P(\tau)/P'(\tau)$ | Importance weight of a trajectory sampled from the proposal | Ch 14 |
| $T_i$, $R_i$ | The $i$-th of several candidate models in robust dynamic programming | Ch 14 |
| $R'$, $\lambda$ | Adversarial reward, and its weight on the log-likelihood of the adversary's choices | Ch 14 |

## Part III: model uncertainty {#part3}

| Symbol | Meaning | First used |
|---|---|---|
| $\theta_a$, $\theta^*$ | Payoff probability of bandit arm $a$; the best arm's | Ch 15 |
| $w_a$, $\ell_a$ | Wins and losses observed on arm $a$ | Ch 15 |
| $\rho_a$ | Posterior probability that the next pull of arm $a$ wins, $(w_a + 1)/(w_a + \ell_a + 2)$ | Ch 15 |
| $\varepsilon$, $\lambda$, $\alpha$, $c$ | Exploration parameters: ε-greedy rate, softmax precision, quantile level, UCB1 constant | Ch 15 |
| $N(a)$, $N$ | Pulls of arm $a$ (here Beta pseudocounts), and their total | Ch 15 |
| $U^*_r$, $Q^*_r$ | Bayes-optimal bandit values with $r$ pulls remaining | Ch 15 |
| $N(s, a, s')$, $N(s, a)$ | Transition counts, and how often $a$ was tried in $s$ | Ch 16 |
| $\rho(s, a)$ | Sum of rewards received for $a$ in $s$ | Ch 16 |
| $\hat T$, $\hat R$ | Estimated (maximum likelihood) transition and reward functions | Ch 16 |
| $m$, $r_{\max}$ | R-MAX's visit threshold and the largest possible reward | Ch 16 |
| $\mathrm{Dir}(\theta \mid \boldsymbol\alpha)$ | Dirichlet distribution over probability vectors, with pseudocounts $\boldsymbol\alpha$ | Ch 16 |
| $b$, $\tau(s, b, a, s')$ | Belief over models, and its Bayes update in a Bayes-adaptive MDP | Ch 16 |
| $\alpha(m)$, $\alpha$ | Learning rate: how far an estimate moves toward each new sample | Ch 17 |
| $\hat x_m$ | Incremental estimate of a mean after $m$ samples | Ch 17 |
| $\delta$ | Temporal difference error, e.g. $r + \gamma Q(s', a') - Q(s, a)$ | Ch 17 |
| $N(s, a)$ (traces) | Eligibility trace: a decaying count of recent visits (not the Ch 16 transition count) | Ch 17 |
| $\lambda$ (traces) | Trace decay parameter in Sarsa(λ) | Ch 17 |
| $F(s, a, s')$, $\beta(s)$ | Shaping reward, and the potential function that makes it safe | Ch 17 |
| $Q_\theta(s, a)$ | Parameterized action value function | Ch 17 |
| $m_{\text{grad}}$ | Batch size for experience replay | Ch 17 |
| $\mathcal{D}$ | Expert demonstrations (state-action pairs or trajectories) | Ch 18 |
| $\pi_E$ | The expert's policy | Ch 18 |
| $\beta(s, a)$, $\phi$ | Reward features and weights: $R_\phi(s, a) = \phi^\top\beta(s, a)$ | Ch 18 |
| $\mu_\pi$, $\mu_E$ | Feature expectations of a policy, and of the expert | Ch 18 |
| $t$ | Margin in maximum margin IRL | Ch 18 |
| $\lambda_i$ | Mixture weights over the policies found by maximum margin IRL | Ch 18 |
| $\beta$ (SMILe) | Mixing rate in SMILe (not the features) | Ch 18 |
| $P_\phi(\tau)$, $Z(\phi)$ | Maximum entropy trajectory distribution and its normalizer | Ch 18 |
| $C_\phi(s, a)$ | GAIL discriminator: probability a pair came from the learner | Ch 18 |

|---|---|---|

| $O(o \mid a, s')$ | Observation model: probability of observing $o$ after taking $a$ and landing in $s'$ | Ch 19 |
| $b(s)$ | Belief: probability that the current state is $s$, given the history | Ch 19 |

| $\mathbf{T}_s$, $\mathbf{T}_a$, $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_s$ | Linear-Gaussian dynamics: state matrix, action matrix, process-noise covariance | Ch 19 |
| $\mathbf{O}_s$, $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_o$ | Linear-Gaussian sensor: observation matrix, sensor-noise covariance | Ch 19 |
| $\boldsymbol{\mu}_b$, $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_b$ | Mean and covariance of a Gaussian belief | Ch 19 |
| $\boldsymbol{\mu}_p$, $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_p$ | Mean and covariance after the predict step | Ch 19 |
| $\mathbf{K}$ | Kalman gain | Ch 19 |
| $s^{(i)}$, $w^{(i)}$ | The $i$-th particle and its weight | Ch 19 |
| $\text{Update}(b, a, o)$ | The belief after acting and observing (the Ch 19 filter) | Ch 20 |
| $R(b, a)$, $T(b' \mid b, a)$ | Reward and transition of the belief-state MDP | Ch 20 |
| $P(o \mid b, a)$ | Probability of observing $o$ after taking $a$ from belief $b$ | Ch 20 |
| $\pi()$, $\pi(o)$ | A conditional plan's root action, and its subplan after observation $o$ | Ch 20 |
| $\alpha_\pi$, $\Gamma$ | Alpha vector of a plan (utility per state), and a set of them | Ch 20 |
| $U^\Gamma(b)$ | $\max_{\alpha \in \Gamma} \alpha^\top b$, the value represented by $\Gamma$ | Ch 20 |
| $\delta$ (pruning) | Largest lead of an alpha vector over a set, over all beliefs | Ch 20 |
| $\mu_b$, $K$ | Belief mean and linear feedback gain in LQG control | Ch 20 |
| $U_{\text{hi}}$, $U_{\text{lo}}$ | Upper and lower bounds on the optimal value over beliefs | Ch 21 |
| $r_{\text{baws}}$ | Best-action worst-state lower bound | Ch 21 |
| $B$ | A finite set of beliefs used by point-based methods | Ch 21 |
| $\alpha_{a,o}$ | The best existing alpha vector after action $a$ and observation $o$ | Ch 21 |
| $V$, $u_E$ | Stored belief-utility pairs (sawtooth), and the corner beliefs' utilities | Ch 21 |
| $\rho(b, b')$ | Minimum ratio $\min_i b_i/b'_i$ in the sawtooth bound | Ch 21 |
| $m$, $\lambda_i$ | Grid granularity and interpolation weights of a triangulation | Ch 21 |
| $\delta$ (gap) | Gap below which heuristic search stops refining a belief | Ch 21 |
| $Q_d(b, a)$, $U_d(b)$ | Forward-search action value and value with $d$ steps left | Ch 22 |
| $m$ (online) | Samples per action (sparse sampling), simulations (MCTS) or scenarios (determinized search) | Ch 22 |
| $h$ | A history: the actions and observations since the current belief | Ch 22 |
| $N(h, a)$, $Q(h, a)$ | Visit count and value estimate of action $a$ after history $h$ (MCTS) | Ch 22 |
| $\Phi$, $\phi = (s, i, j)$ | Determinizing matrix of uniform numbers; a particle's state, scenario and depth | Ch 22 |
| $X$, $x$ | A controller's nodes, and one node (its memory state, not the environment's state) | Ch 23 |
| $\psi(a \mid x)$ | A controller's action distribution at node $x$ | Ch 23 |
| $\eta(x' \mid x, a, o)$ | A controller's successor distribution after action $a$ and observation $o$ | Ch 23 |
| $U(x, s)$, $\alpha_x$ | Value of node $x$ in state $s$; node $x$'s alpha vector | Ch 23 |
| $T_\theta$, $r_\theta$, $u_\theta$ | Transition matrix, rewards and values on (node, state) pairs for controller parameters $\theta = (\psi, \eta)$ | Ch 23 |
| $\beta$, $v$ | Start distribution on (node, state) pairs; expected discounted time spent in each pair | Ch 23 |
| $\tau$ | Shift in the projection onto the probability simplex | Ch 23 |

## Part V: multiagent systems {#part5}

| Symbol | Meaning | First used |
|---|---|---|
| $\mathcal{I}$, $i$, $k$ | The agents, one agent, and their number | Ch 24 |
| $\mathcal{A}^i$, $\boldsymbol{a} = (a^1, \dots, a^k)$ | Agent $i$'s actions; a joint action | Ch 24 |
| $-i$ | Every agent except $i$, as in $\boldsymbol{a}^{-i}$ or $\boldsymbol{\pi}^{-i}$ | Ch 24 |
| $R^i(\boldsymbol{a})$ | Agent $i$'s reward for the joint action $\boldsymbol{a}$ | Ch 24 |
| $\pi^i(a^i)$, $\boldsymbol{\pi}$ | Agent $i$'s policy (a pure or mixed strategy); the joint policy | Ch 24 |
| $U^i(\boldsymbol{\pi})$ | Agent $i$'s expected reward under the joint policy | Ch 24 |
| $\pi(\boldsymbol{a})$ (correlated) | A single distribution over joint actions | Ch 24 |
| $\lambda$, $k$ (hierarchical softmax) | Precision of the softmax response; level of reasoning | Ch 24 |
| $N^i(j, a^j)$ | Agent $i$'s count of how often agent $j$ played $a^j$ (fictitious play) | Ch 24 |
| $\pi^i(a^i \mid s)$ | Agent $i$'s state-dependent policy in a Markov game | Ch 25 |
| $R^i(s, \boldsymbol{a})$, $T(s' \mid s, \boldsymbol{a})$ | Agent $i$'s reward and the shared transition model, given the joint action | Ch 25 |
| $U^{\boldsymbol{\pi}, i}(s)$ | Agent $i$'s value of state $s$ under the joint policy | Ch 25 |
| $Q^i(s, \boldsymbol{a})$ | Agent $i$'s value of a joint action in state $s$ | Ch 25 |
| $N(j, a^j, s)$ | Count of agent $j$ playing $a^j$ in state $s$ (fictitious play) | Ch 25 |
| $\boldsymbol{o} = (o^1, \dots, o^k)$, $O(\boldsymbol{o} \mid \boldsymbol{a}, s')$ | A joint observation, and its probability after joint action $\boldsymbol{a}$ | Ch 26 |
| $\boldsymbol{\pi}()$, $\boldsymbol{\pi}(\boldsymbol{o})$ | Joint conditional plan's root actions; each agent's subplan after its own observation | Ch 26 |
| $\Pi^i_h$ | Agent $i$'s set of $h$-step conditional plans | Ch 26 |
| $b(\boldsymbol{\pi}^{-i}, s)$ | Distribution over the other agents' plans and the state (pruning LP) | Ch 26 |
| $\boldsymbol{x} = (x^1, \dots, x^k)$ | Joint controller node | Ch 26 |
| $R(s, \boldsymbol{a})$ (shared) | The team's single reward in a Dec-POMDP | Ch 27 |
| $U^*_{\text{MPOMDP}}(b)$ | Optimal team value if observations were shared (an upper bound) | Ch 27 |

## Appendices {#appendices}

| Symbol | Meaning | First used |
|---|---|---|
| $\lVert \mathbf{x} \rVert_p$ | The $p$-norm of a vector; $\lVert \mathbf{x} \rVert_\infty$ is its largest absolute entry | App A |
| $\mathbf{A} \succ 0$ | $\mathbf{A}$ is positive definite: $\mathbf{x}^\top \mathbf{A} \mathbf{x} > 0$ for every $\mathbf{x} \ne \mathbf{0}$ | App A |
| $H(P)$, $H(P, Q)$ | Entropy of $P$; cross entropy of $Q$ relative to $P$ | App A |
| $\nabla f(\mathbf{x})$ | Gradient: the vector of partial derivatives, pointing uphill | App A |
| $B$ | The Bellman backup as an operator on value functions | App A |
| $O(g(n))$, $\Omega(g(n))$, $\Theta(g(n))$ | Grows no faster than, no slower than, and as fast as $g$, up to constant factors | App C |
| $\mathbf{W}$, $\mathbf{b}$, $\phi$ | A network layer's weights, biases and activation function | App D |
| $\operatorname{softmax}(\mathbf{z})$ | Turns scores into probabilities: $e^{z_i}/\sum_j e^{z_j}$ | App D |
| $\beta$ (regularization) | Weight of the penalty on squared network weights | App D |
| $\mathcal{A}(s)$ | Valid actions in state $s$ (none in an absorbing state) | App E |
| $T(s, a)$ (deterministic) | The one next state after taking $a$ in $s$ | App E |

: Symbols introduced in the appendices. {#tbl-notation-app}

## Symbols with several meanings {#overloaded}

The book, and so this site, reuses a few letters. The chapter always makes the meaning clear, but when reading across chapters, check this list.

| Symbol | Meanings, by chapter |
|---|---|
| $\alpha$ | Pseudocounts (Ch 4–5, 16); step size (Ch 10, App A); quantile level (Ch 15); learning rate (Ch 17); alpha vector (Ch 20–23) |
| $\beta$ | Beta parameter (Ch 4); basis functions (Ch 8); shaping potential (Ch 17); reward features and SMILe rate (Ch 18); start distribution (Ch 23); regularization weight (App D) |
| $\delta$ | Residual thresholds (Ch 7, 9); finite-difference step (Ch 11); temporal difference residual (Ch 13, 17); pruning lead (Ch 20); belief gap (Ch 21) |
| $\lambda$ | Risk aversion (Ch 6); GAE weight (Ch 13); adversary weight (Ch 14); softmax precision (Ch 15, 24); trace decay (Ch 17); interpolation and mixture weights (Ch 18, 21) |
| $\phi$ | Factor (Ch 3); kernel (Ch 4); critic parameters (Ch 13); reward weights (Ch 18); particle (Ch 22); activation function (App D) |
| $b$ | Initial state distribution (Ch 10, 14); belief over models (Ch 16); belief over states (Ch 19 on) |
| $m$ | Counts (Ch 4–5); number of samples or simulations (Ch 9, 22); R-MAX threshold (Ch 16); grid granularity (Ch 21) |
| $h$ | Hidden variables (Ch 3); kernel bandwidth (Ch 4); history (Ch 22); plan horizon (Ch 26) |
| $N$ | Visit counts (Ch 9, 15, 16, 22); eligibility traces (Ch 17); opponent action counts (Ch 24, 25) |

: Letters that mean different things in different chapters. {#tbl-overloaded}
